text: HTTP/1.1 keeps connections open by default (keep-alive), so repeated polls usually reuse one TCP/TLS connection. Only 'Connection: close' or an idle timeout ends it. HTTP/1.0 opened a new connection per request.
why: Corrects the 'new handshake per poll' assumption.

text: TCP closes each direction independently: a FIN from one side is ACKed, then a FIN from the other side is ACKed (four segments), and the side that closed first waits in TIME-WAIT for 2xMSL.
Keep long-poll timeouts modest: RFC 6202 notes that too-long waits can be cut by proxies with 408/504 and suggests about 30 seconds as a safe value.
Amazon SQS exposes long polling as a parameter: ReceiveMessage with WaitTimeSeconds > 0 (max 20 s) returns as soon as a message is available.

The WebSocket handshake is an HTTP/1.1 GET with 'Upgrade: websocket' and 'Connection: Upgrade'. The server answers '101 Switching Protocols', and from then on the TCP connection carries WebSocket frames.
why: Shows how WS relates to HTTP.

text: RFC 8441 lets a WebSocket run over a single stream of an HTTP/2 connection (extended CONNECT), so one TCP connection can carry both HTTP/2 requests and WebSockets.
WebSocket frames have a 2-byte minimum header (up to 14 bytes with extended length and masking), and every client-to-server frame must be masked.
WebSocket defines Ping and Pong control frames, used as keepalives or to check that the peer is still responsive.

Browsers' EventSource reconnects automatically. On reconnect it sends a Last-Event-ID header with the last 'id:' it saw, so the server can resume the stream. The server can set the delay with a 'retry:' field.
A server can tell an SSE client to stop reconnecting by responding with HTTP 204 No Content.
Over HTTP/1.1, browsers allow only about 6 concurrent connections per domain, shared across tabs, which SSE streams quickly exhaust. Over HTTP/2 the streams are multiplexed (default ~100).
SSE streams use MIME type text/event-stream and must be UTF-8 text. There is no binary framing as in WebSockets.
Proxies may drop idle HTTP connections. The SSE spec suggests sending a comment line (starting with ':') about every 15 seconds to keep the stream alive.

Idle timeouts differ by layer: AWS ALB defaults to 60 s, AWS NLB TCP listeners to 350 s, nginx proxy_read_timeout to 60 s. Long-lived connections need heartbeats (e.g. WebSocket pings) or tuned timeouts.
why: Why L4 vs L7 matters for long-lived connections.

text: An L7 proxy must forward the hop-by-hop Upgrade and Connection headers for a WebSocket to work. nginx does not pass them by default, so they must be set explicitly.
With AWS ALB, an upgraded WebSocket becomes a persistent connection between the client and one target through the load balancer, so a single WebSocket is pinned to one backend automatically.

Socket.IO is not a WebSocket implementation. It adds its own packet metadata and falls back to HTTP long-polling, so a plain WebSocket client cannot connect to a Socket.IO server. Its client reconnects automatically with exponential backoff.
Running Socket.IO on multiple nodes needs sticky sessions when HTTP long-polling is enabled (a session spans several HTTP requests), plus an adapter (e.g. Redis) to broadcast across nodes.
Retries during overload make it worse. Add exponential backoff with jitter so reconnects spread out over time instead of arriving as one synchronized storm.

A TCP connection is identified by its 4-tuple (source IP and port, destination IP and port). Ephemeral-port limits constrain the connecting side, while one server port can hold millions of connections; WhatsApp reported over 2 million per server.
why: Correct mental model of connection limits.

text: QUIC (RFC 9000) is a connection-oriented, stateful transport carried in UDP datagrams, with streams and connection migration. HTTP/3 (RFC 9114) runs over it, avoiding TCP head-of-line blocking that affects HTTP/2.
why: Persistent connections are not TCP-only; HTTP version context.

text: HTTP/2 multiplexes many concurrent requests over one connection, which further reduces per-request connection cost for polling clients.
why: HTTP version context for polling overhead.

text: APNs is best-effort: it may reorder notifications, stores only one pending notification per app, and may throttle. Providers should keep HTTP/2 connections to APNs open and reuse them for hours to days.

GCM server and client APIs were deprecated in April 2018 and removed starting April 11, 2019; Firebase Cloud Messaging is the replacement. FCM delivers via Android's transport layer, APNs for Apple devices, and Web Push for browsers.
MQTT is a client/server publish/subscribe protocol that runs over TCP/IP or any ordered, lossless, bi-directional transport. MQTT 5.0 defines WebSocket as one such transport.
